question: A 31-year-old G2P2002 delivers a male child at 40 weeks gestation after an uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery. The newborn is vigorous at birth with Apgar scores of 7 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The mother has a first-degree laceration that is hemostatically repaired, and the two are transferred to the postpartum unit for routine care. The mother has a past medical history of chronic hepatitis C from intravenous drug use, for which she attended inpatient rehabilitation several times. She last used drugs three years ago. During her prenatal care, her HIV test was negative. She has no other past medical history, and her family history is notable only for hypertension and colorectal cancer. Her partner has a history of recurrent cold sores and no significant family history. Which of the following is the best feeding method for this newborn?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Newborn is vigorous at birth" -> "Apgar scores of 7 and 9 indicate good health" -> "Breastfeeding is recommended for healthy newborns" -> "Mother has chronic hepatitis C but is not actively using drugs" -> "Breastfeeding is safe with chronic hepatitis C" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Newborn is vigorous at birth" -> "Apgar scores of 7 and 9 indicate good health" -> "Breastfeeding provides optimal nutrition" -> "Mother's hepatitis C is well-managed" -> "No contraindications for breastfeeding" -> 90%

enhanced_information: The newborn is vigorous at birth with good Apgar scores, indicating overall health. Breastfeeding is recommended for healthy newborns as it provides optimal nutrition and immune support. The mother has chronic hepatitis C but is not actively using drugs, and current guidelines indicate that breastfeeding is safe for mothers with well-managed hepatitis C, as the virus is not transmitted through breast milk. Therefore, the best feeding method for this newborn is breastfeeding. Donated breast milk is a viable alternative if breastfeeding is not possible, but in this case, the mother is capable of breastfeeding.
